evidence: Judged "If it won't step back" over "That part doesn't have to move out. It's been living there way longer than the grown-up you...". "it" is the guard, as in the heading above it, and "step back" picks up the section's opening question "What are you afraid would happen if you stepped back?"; the paragraph answers the heading at once ("That part doesn't have to move out") and covers the refusal itself ("If it says no, I'd listen"), so it promises nothing the paragraph lacks and adds no claim. GATE-INPUTS-R3 lists no linter findings and no writer-marked rows, and I find no tell row operating: reusing "step back" ties the case to that opening question, so it is not unearned T26, and it is a plain conditional label, not T19 or T12. Beside the other three headings it reads as one more snag in Joel's own run of paragraphs, not a coverage taxonomy.
